title: Pandas
description: Learn how to manipulate, clean, and analyze real-world datasets using Pandas.
objectives: Load data from CSV and Excel into a DataFrame and inspect it.
Select, filter, and sort rows and columns confidently.
Aggregate with groupby and combine tables with merge.
Detect and handle missing values, and work with datetime columns.

slides.title: Pandas
slides.lead: Pandas is where most of a data analyst's day is spent. It is NumPy with labels, missing-value handling, and tables.
bullets: Series  one labelled column
DataFrame  a whole labelled table
Load, clean, filter, group, join, summarise
Import convention: import pandas as pd

slides.title: Series  a labelled 1D array
slides.lead: A Series is a NumPy array plus an index. Every column of a DataFrame is a Series.
bullets: Created from a list, dict, or NumPy array
The index labels each value and defaults to 0, 1, 2…
Vectorised math works exactly as it does in NumPy
.value_counts() counts occurrences  the most used method in Pandas
Operations align on the index, not on position

slides.title: DataFrame  the table
slides.lead: A DataFrame is a dict of Series sharing one index. Rows are records, columns are fields.
bullets: df.head() / df.tail()  look at the ends
df.shape  (rows, columns)
df.info()  dtypes and non-null counts in one view
df.describe()  count, mean, std, quartiles for numeric columns
df.columns  the column labels
slides.note: df.info() is the first thing to run on any new dataset  it shows dtypes and missing counts together.

slides.title: GroupBy  split, apply, combine
slides.lead: Split rows into groups by a column, apply a summary to each group, then combine the results into a new table.
bullets: df.groupby("class")["score"].mean()
Group by several columns for a nested breakdown
.agg() applies different functions to different columns
Common: sum, mean, count, min, max, nunique
reset_index() turns the group labels back into columns

slides.title: Merge  joining two tables
slides.lead: merge is a SQL join. Pick the key column and the how, then always check the row count afterwards.

body: pd.merge(students, scores, on="id", how="inner")   # only ids 1, 2
pd.merge(students, scores, on="id", how="left")    # all students, NaN for Mony
pd.merge(students, scores, on="id", how="outer")   # everything, ids 1-4
# different key names on each side

slides.note: If a merge returns more rows than you started with, the key is not unique on one side. Check with df["id"].duplicated().any().

slides.title: Missing values
slides.lead: Real data has holes. Decide deliberately whether to drop them or fill them  never ignore them.
bullets: df.isna().sum()  count missing per column, run this first
df.dropna()  drop rows; subset= limits which columns count
df.fillna(value)  fill with a constant, mean, or median
ffill / bfill carry the previous or next value forward
NaN is a float, so any column containing one becomes float

body: df = df.dropna(subset=["score"])          # a row with no score is useless
# tidy up column names while you are here

slides.note: Filling with the mean pulls the distribution toward the centre and shrinks the variance. Median is safer when the data is skewed.

slides.title: Practice: a full cleaning pass
slides.lead: Take any CSV with at least 200 rows and run this sequence in a notebook.
bullets: Load it, then run .shape, .info(), and .describe()
Normalise the column names to lowercase with underscores
Report missing values per column and decide drop or fill for each
Remove duplicate rows on the identifier column
Group by one categorical column and report count, mean, and max
Export the cleaned table with to_csv(..., index=False)
slides.note: Write one sentence under each step explaining why you made that choice. That commentary is what turns a notebook into a report.

slides.title: Module 04 recap
slides.lead: This is the core analyst skill set  everything after this is presentation.
bullets: Series is a column; DataFrame is a table
Filter with boolean masks; assign through .loc
groupby answers "per category, what is the…" questions
merge joins tables  always verify the row count after
Handle missing values on purpose, and record the decision
